To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phthalates are antiandrogens that can cause obesity and that bisphenol A causes obesity and is an estrogen that can disrupt brain sexual differentiation.

the endocrine disruption paradigm has been extended to the brain and that this has led to the identification of new neurotoxicants and to the recognition that neurotoxicants may have endocrine disruption potential.

phthalate ester anti-androgens are capable of disrupting the sexual differentiation of the developing brain and that this effect is associated with behavioral changes in adulthood, but that there is no evidence that these agents are carcinogenic in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobehavioral effects of endocrine disrupting chemicals.
the effects of environmental toxicants on brain development, particularly the effects of endocrine disrupting chemicals.
the neurodevelopmental and neurobehavioral consequences of environmental chemicals, with a focus on endocrine disruption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EDCs have the potential to affect brain sexual differentiation, but the effects of these agents on brain sexual differentiation are complex and not yet fully understood.
the neurotoxicity of EDCs is a major and growing health concern, one that is not yet fully recognized or understood.
the field of endocrine disruption is a major challenge for the neurotoxicologists of the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endocrine disruption is an important part of our neurotoxicological future.
endocrine disruption is a neurotoxicology problem.

the neurotoxicity of endocrine disruption is not simply a question about the effects of hormones on brain development, but also about the effects of EDCs, which mimic and/or interfere with the actions of those hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Organizational Hypotheses is not just an idea about how the brain is organized during development, but a principle about how the brain and the rest of the body can be altered during development by environmental chemicals.
the Organizational Hypotheses is a useful guide to understanding the neurobehavioral effects of EDCs.
EDCs, and endocrine disruption, are important components of the neurotoxicologist's portfolio.
